_comment: Phase D observations for the 18 score<20 entries. Now augmented with `callers` (gathered via Ghidra MCP get_function_callers) to support caller-aware rule discrimination — primarily for the `__nmemneed` hash-identical family of 7-byte XOR-RET stubs. 0x4d8ea was previously accepted as a real __nmemneed but caller analysis showed its only inbound chain comes from crt_signal_handler_print via a JMP thunk (signal subsystem path, not heap allocator path); rejected as false positive in the post-Phase-D revision.

000353cc.key_instructions: PUSH 0x190 (=400); CALL 0x375b2 (a delay function, NOT fgetc); ADD ESP,0x4; RET
000353cc.notes: Game-side delay(400ms) wrapper for cinematic chapter portrait flash effect. Single caller is a game cinematic function — no CRT pathway. Watcom fgetchar would be `return fgetc(stdin)` and would be called from user main loop or other stdio.
000353cc.manual_reason: Calls a delay function with arg 400ms; no FILE/_iob touch, no fgetc call. Caller is game cinematic logic, not stdio. Behavior fundamentally inconsistent with matched_name.

callers: ...100+ game funcs (compiler-inserted stack-check at every prologue needing >4K stack)
00036cd7.asm:

00036cdb: CALL 0x00036cea

00036cd7.key_instructions: XCHG saves caller's EAX onto stack then loads stack-need into EAX; CALL __STK to probe; restore EAX; RET 0x4
00036cd7.notes: Watcom __CHK entry stub. The very large caller list (100+) is exactly the expected pattern: Watcom compiler emits a CALL __CHK at the prologue of every function whose frame would touch beyond a single guard page. body 16 fits.

00036cea.notes: Standard Watcom __STK: probes that EAX bytes can be allocated on the stack. Sole caller is __CHK — exactly the expected entry-point pair. body 29 fits.

00037821.notes: Watcom getch with ungetch buffer. Single caller is debug_print_ans_and_length — debug pause path. INT 21h AH=0x08 + ungetch stash buffer is a perfect getch signature.

000462d1.asm:
000462d1: CALL 0x0003d7f6
000462d6: MOV dword ptr [EAX],0x9
000462dc: MOV EAX,0xffffffff
000462e1: RET
000462d1.key_instructions: CALL __get_errno_ptr; STORE 0x9 (= EBADF in Watcom errno.h); return -1
000462d1.notes: This is the __EBADF helper, NOT __EINVAL. Watcom errno.h defines EBADF=9 and EINVAL=22 (0x16). FidDb labelled it __EINVAL because the family of set-errno helpers in dosret.obj all hash to identical bytes (the immediate is masked).
000462d1.manual_reason: Function sets errno=9 (EBADF), but matched_name is __EINVAL (would store 0x16). Behavior matches __EBADF in the same dosret.obj family. Mislabeled by FidDb due to imm32-masking.

0004693d.notes: Watcom __full_io_exit: closes all streams (mode 0) then tail-calls __purgefp. No direct callers because it's invoked via atexit/exit indirection (exit handler table), not direct CALL.

0004694c.key_instructions: PUSH 5 (some flags mask); CALL close-streams helper; RET
0004694c.notes: Body 11 with score 4.34 (lowest cluster). Thin wrapper that calls 0x46957 with arg 5. Standard Watcom fcloseall iterates _iob[] and fcloses each open stream (50+ bytes). No iteration here, no _iob field touch. Per crt_fid_match.md §8.3 doc author independently flagged false positive.
0004694c.manual_reason: Body 11 bytes too small for fcloseall's expected _iob[] loop. No iteration, no _iob field access. Generic 'PUSH imm + CALL helper' pattern that hashes weakly (4.34) to fcloseall's signature.

0004d8ea.asm:
0004d8ea: PUSH EBP
0004d8eb: MOV EBP,ESP
0004d8ed: XOR EAX,EAX
0004d8ef: POP EBP
0004d8f0: RET
0004d8ea.key_instructions: PUSH EBP / MOV EBP,ESP / XOR EAX,EAX / POP EBP / RET — return 0
0004d8ea.notes: Body byte-identical to 0x3d6f2 (the real __nmemneed). FidDb hash family contains every CLIB3S 7-byte XOR-RET stub (signal default, nmemneed default, etc.) since they're literally the same bytes. Caller analysis is the discriminator: 0x3d6f2 is called directly by `_nmalloc` (heap path); 0x4d8ea has no direct caller — only an UNCONDITIONAL_JUMP from `0x4d340` which is itself called by `crt_signal_handler_print` (signal subsystem path). This entry is a different default-zero stub in the signal subsystem, not __nmemneed.
0004d8ea.manual_reason: Caller analysis: 0x4d8ea reached only via JMP from 0x4d340 -> crt_signal_handler_print (signal subsystem), not from _nmalloc / heap allocator path. Real __nmemneed (0x3d6f2) IS called by _nmalloc. Same byte pattern, different role. Renamed in Ghidra to noop_stub_4d8ea_zero to match its sibling thunk noop_stub_4d340_zero.
